newsitem.title: CHINA: Record number of Chinese go abroad in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Record number of Chinese go abroad in 1996.

text.p: China's Public Security Ministry issued a record number of passports to people travelling abroad at their own expense after it loosened restrictions on overseas trips, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
Some 2.4 million people went abroad at private expense last year, it said. Many Chinese travel on government passports rather than at their own cost on private documents.
After the ministry loosened restrictions on Chinese going abroad for private reasons and simplified procedures, the number of people applying to travel increased sharply, the ministry said.
The number of people going to Hong Kong and Macau fell last year, but travellers to Taiwan, an island that Beijing regards as a renegade province, soared 20 percent to 51,000, it said.

Most of the individual travelers were from coastal and border provinces, such as southwestern Yunnan, southern Guangdong, northeastern Heilongjiang and Beijing. Most popular destinations were the United States, Thailand, Japan, South Korea, Australia and Singapore, it said.
